p_documentation: Edit the language JSON and templates in `.readme/` and `.changelog/`, then regenerate the documents. Do not edit generated Markdown directly. The root README uses Simplified Chinese. These commands require Python 3.10 or newer without extra Python packages; Windows can use `py` instead of `python`. `--check` validates languages, fields, historical versions and dates, punctuation, and generated files without writing. CI runs the same check.
vscode002: A [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/) extension for debugging and running [AutoJs6](https://github.com/SuperMonster003/AutoJs6) scripts
vscode007: Select "AutoJs6 VSCode Extension" and install or update it
vscode009: Connect devices in VSCode and manage AutoJs6 scripts or projects (run, stop, save, etc.)
vscode010: Display AutoJs6 logs in real time in VSCode
vscode011: Connect by QR code and discover devices running server mode on the local network (AutoJs6 6.8.0+)
vscode012: Pairing confirmation asks before accepting an unknown device, trusts QR-paired devices automatically, and lets you manage trusted devices
vscode013: Browse, edit, upload, download and delete device files, run device scripts, and transfer large files in chunks with progress (AutoJs6 6.8.0+)
vscode014: Pull project changes from a device (device edits -> local files, with per-file diff previews)
vscode015: Heartbeats, automatic reconnection and a status-bar device indicator
vscode016: A local HTTP command bridge lets external tools invoke extension commands
vscode017: Interface text follows the VSCode display language (Simplified Chinese / English), or can be pinned through `autojs6.language`
vscode025: Buttons at the top of the VSCode title area provide quick file/project operations
vscode027: Open `< Command Palette >` and select `AutoJs6: Connect` `[ Ctrl+Alt+F6 ]`, or click the corresponding menu button
vscode028: Choose one of the following connection methods
vscode030: Enable "Client mode" in the AutoJs6 drawer
vscode031: Enter a local IP address shown by VSCode (the extension listens on `6347`; allow it through the firewall and change it with `autojs6.server.port`)
vscode033: VSCode displays the connection QR code for this computer; you can switch network interfaces
vscode034: In the AutoJs6 (6.8.0+) drawer, select "Client mode" and use the scan button beside the address field to scan the code and connect automatically
vscode036: Enable "Server mode" in the AutoJs6 drawer (listening on `7347`)
vscode037: In VSCode, enter the IP address or hostname of the AutoJs6 device, optionally with a port (such as `192.168.1.5:7347` or `[fe80::1]:7347`)
vscode038: After an unexpected disconnect, the extension reconnects automatically with exponential backoff for 5 minutes by default (disable with `autojs6.connection.autoReconnect`); VSCode restores the last connection after restarting (`autojs6.connection.restoreOnStartup`)
vscode039: An explicit disconnect from either side (VSCode commands or the AutoJs6 drawer/manager) stops automatic reconnection
vscode041: Enable "Server mode" in the AutoJs6 drawer
vscode042: Connect the AutoJs6 device to the computer running VSCode through USB
vscode043: Enable USB debugging on the AutoJs6 device and allow it to trust the computer
vscode044: The procedure varies by device; consult its manufacturer's manual or relevant online documentation
vscode046: Successful device IP addresses are saved in a selection list
vscode048: A device's IP address may change
vscode049: Use "Clear" to remove all saved records
vscode050: A VSCode message `AutoJs6 device connected: ${DEVICE} (${IP_ADDRESS})` confirms the connection
vscode052: Open `< Command Palette >` to view and run supported commands; shortcuts are listed under "Commands" below
vscode053: For example, `AutoJs6: Run` and `AutoJs6: Stop All`
vscode054: Some operations also have corresponding menu buttons
vscode056: Choose one of the following ways to view logs from AutoJs6
vscode057: Use the `OUTPUT` panel `[ F12 ]` opened after connecting; each device has its own panel
vscode058: Click the `AutoJs6: N` status-bar indicator, select a device and choose "Show logs"
vscode059: After disconnection, the panel is retained and marked disconnected by default; `autojs6.log.disposeChannelOnDisconnect` can remove it automatically
vscode060: Enable the extension's own debug logs through `autojs6.log.debug`; they appear in `AutoJs6 VSCode Extension Debug`
vscode062: Click the `AutoJs6` activity-bar icon and browse connected devices' working directories and external storage in "Device Files (Device Files)"
vscode063: Click a file to open it in the editor; saving in VSCode writes changes directly back to the device
vscode064: Context menus and inline buttons run scripts, create folders/files, upload current or local files, download, rename and delete
vscode065: Choose "Upload folders here (Upload Folders)" on a device directory to select multiple local folders. Selected names, subdirectories and empty directories are preserved; existing directories are merged, matching files overwritten, and other device files retained. Uploads show the current path and support cancellation while keeping uploaded content; symlinks and unsupported file types are skipped with a notice
vscode066: `AutoJs6: Browse Device Files` adds a device directory to Explorer as a workspace folder
vscode068: Choose one of the following ways to close all connections between AutoJs6 and VSCode
vscode069: Open `< Command Palette >` and select `AutoJs6: Disconnect All` `[ Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F6 ]`
vscode070: Turn off the relevant client/server switch in the AutoJs6 drawer
vscode071: Disconnect the USB connection of AutoJs6 (only for ADB (USB) connections)
vscode072: Exit the AutoJs6 app or close VSCode
vscode074: View online documentation (View Online Document) `[ Alt+Shift+F6 ]`
vscode075: Open the AutoJs6 online developer documentation
vscode078: The relevant AutoJs6 switches may need manual enablement
vscode079: Show connection QR code (Show QR Code) `[ CTRL+ALT+6 Q ]`
vscode080: Show a QR code for the AutoJs6 client mode to scan
vscode083: The relevant AutoJs6 switches may be reset
vscode087: Retry a reconnecting target immediately, or restore the last successful LAN/ADB connection
vscode090: Pull project changes from a device (Pull Project from Device)
vscode091: Compare the device copy with the local project, select new/modified device files to pull, and preview each diff
vscode093: View and remove trusted AutoJs6 devices; a removed device requires confirmation the next time it connects
vscode095: List connected devices and choose an action (logs, run, save, browse files or disconnect), also available through the status-bar indicator
vscode097: Run the script corresponding to the current VSCode
vscode100: Stop and rerun the script corresponding to the current VSCode
vscode102: Stop the script corresponding to the current VSCode
vscode106: Save the current file to the AutoJs6 working directory of connected devices
vscode107: Run on a selected device (Run On Device)
vscode108: Open the device menu and choose where to run the script corresponding to VSCode
vscode109: Save to a selected device (Save To Device)
vscode110: Open the device menu and choose where to save the script corresponding to VSCode
vscode112: Select an empty folder, creating one if needed, for a new AutoJs6 project
vscode113: After creating a project, run `npm run dts-link` or `npm run dts` to deploy declarations
vscode114: Run project (Run Project) `[ CTRL+ALT+6 R / Alt+F6 ]`
vscode116: Save project to device (Save Project) `[ CTRL+ALT+6 S ]`
vscode117: Save an AutoJs6 project incrementally; propagating file deletions to the device requires AutoJs6 6.8.0+
vscode119: Send every project file to the device and overwrite matching files
vscode121: Add a device directory to Explorer as a workspace folder (AutoJs6 6.8.0+)
vscode124: | `autojs6.language` | `auto` | Interface language: `auto` follows the VSCode display language; `en` or `zh-cn` pins it. Command titles and setting descriptions always follow VSCode; reload the window to apply every change |
vscode125: | `autojs6.server.port` | `6347` | Extension listening port, used by AutoJs6 client mode |
vscode126: | `autojs6.server.confirmUnknownDevices` | `true` | Ask before accepting an unknown client-mode device; QR-paired or previously allowed-and-remembered devices need no confirmation |
vscode127: | `autojs6.client.port` | `7347` | Default port for AutoJs6 server mode |
vscode128: | `autojs6.http.enabled` / `autojs6.http.host` / `autojs6.http.port` | `true` / `127.0.0.1` / `10347` | Local HTTP command bridge, for example `http://127.0.0.1:10347/exec?cmd=run&path=...` |
vscode129: | `autojs6.adb.path` | Empty | Path to the adb executable or its directory; an empty value enables autodetection |
vscode130: | `autojs6.discovery.enabled` | `true` | Discover AutoJs6 6.8.0+ devices running server mode through mDNS (`_autojs6._tcp`) when connecting over LAN |
vscode131: | `autojs6.connection.connectTimeout` / `handshakeTimeout` | `8000` / `6000` | Connection and handshake timeouts in milliseconds |
vscode132: | `autojs6.connection.heartbeatInterval` / `heartbeatTimeout` | `15000` / `10000` | Heartbeat interval and timeout in milliseconds; interval 0 disables heartbeats |
vscode133: | `autojs6.connection.autoReconnect` / `maxReconnectAttempts` | `true` / `0` | Reconnect unexpected disconnections of extension-initiated connections; 0 attempts means unlimited |
vscode134: | `autojs6.connection.reconnectTimeout` / `reconnectMaxDelay` | `300` / `10000` | Reconnection-session window in seconds (0 means unlimited) and maximum backoff in milliseconds |
vscode135: | `autojs6.connection.restoreOnStartup` | `true` | Restore the last successful device connection at VSCode startup, except explicit disconnections |
vscode136: | `autojs6.log.showChannelOnConnect` | `true` | Show the log panel automatically when a device connects |
vscode137: | `autojs6.log.disposeChannelOnDisconnect` | `false` | Remove the log panel when a device disconnects |
vscode139: | `autojs6.save.keepRelativePath` | `true` | Preserve workspace-relative directories when saving files (AutoJs6 6.8.0+) |
